back: Reducing the number of bits needed to store a file, saving storage space, bandwidth and time.
Compression after which the original file can be restored exactly.
Compression that permanently removes some data (the least noticeable), giving a smaller file that cannot be restored exactly.

front: When to use lossless or lossy
back: Lossless where every bit matters (programs, text, medical images). Lossy where a smaller file matters more than exact detail (photographs, music, video for the web).
A lossless method that replaces each run of identical items with a count and the item, e.g. AAAB becomes 3A1B.

front: When does RLE not save space?
back: When the data has few or no repeated neighbours (such as a photograph or ordinary text), because every item becomes a count-and-item pair.
Original size ÷ compressed size. Percentage saving = (original − compressed) ÷ original × 100.
Removes sounds the human ear is unlikely to notice, such as very high frequencies or quiet sounds masked by louder ones.
Dictionary methods replace repeated words with short references; Huffman coding gives common characters shorter codes. Both are lossless.
